transcript.text: G'day, got a crack in the windscreen from a stone. Can I claim that?

G'day, I'm Sam, Wattle Car Insurance's AI claims assistant. You can talk to a person at any time. Just ask.

Sorry to hear about the windscreen. You can report it and I can help you lodge it now. Whether it's covered depends on your policy. A claims consultant confirms that when they review the claim. Whether to claim is up to you, and I can put you through to someone if you'd like to talk it over first.

First, is anyone hurt, or are you somewhere unsafe right now?
Nah, all good mate, no one's hurt. I'm parked up at home now.
Good to hear. Next I need to confirm who you are. What's your policy number? If you don't have it handy, your date of birth and mobile number will work too.
Yeah, I've got it, it's in one of the emails. Think it's WTL... something. Hang on, I'll grab it.
No rush. Send it through once you've found it.
Cheers. Found it, it's WTL456809.

Thanks, Tane, you're verified. I can see your 2019 Mitsubishi Triton, rego 109TWA, on a Comprehensive policy. I'll lodge the claim for that car.

When did the stone hit the windscreen? Give me the date and roughly what time.
Saturday, the 24th. Think it was around 3pm, sometime in the arvo.
That's Saturday 24 October 2026, at about 3pm. Is that right?
Yeah, that's right, Saturday arvo, round 3.
Thanks. Where were you when it happened? The street and suburb is enough, or the closest road if you were on a highway.
Bruce Highway, up near Caboolture. Heading north, I think.

Got it: Bruce Highway near Caboolture, heading north.

You mentioned a stone hit the windscreen and cracked it. Is that right?
Yep, a stone flicked up off a truck and cracked the windscreen. Driver's side, about 20cm long and it's spreading a bit.
Thanks, I've noted that. Who was driving at the time?
Me, I was driving. Just me in the car.
Thanks. Is the car safe to drive right now? A crack on the driver's side that's spreading can block your view or get worse. If you're not sure, just say so.
Yeah, I'm still driving it, it's been fine. Haven't noticed it spreading much since Saturday, though it does look a bit bigger than it did. Probably should get it looked at soon.

Thanks. I'll record it as drivable. Getting it checked soon is a good idea, because cracks can grow quickly with heat and bumps.

For the description, here's what I have: a stone flicked up off a truck and cracked the windscreen on the driver's side. The crack is about 20cm long and has grown a little since Saturday. Is that right, and is there any other damage?
Yep, that's about right. Didn't notice any other damage, just the windscreen. Paint's fine and the wipers still work.
Thanks. Did you get any details of the truck, like the company name, the rego or what it looked like? If not, that's fine.
Nah, didn't get anything. It was a big truck, I think white or grey, and it just kept going. Didn't stop.
No worries, I'll note that. Did you report it to the police and get a reference number? Most people don't for a windscreen, so it's fine if you didn't.
Nah, didn't call the cops or anything. Didn't seem worth it for a windscreen.

Here's a summary of your claim:

- **Car:** 2019 Mitsubishi Triton, rego 109TWA
- **When:** Saturday 24 October 2026, about 3pm
- **Where:** Bruce Highway near Caboolture, heading north
- **Type:** Windscreen damage
- **Driver:** Tane Walker
- **Drivable:** Yes
- **What happened:** A stone flicked up from a truck and cracked the windscreen on the driver's side. The crack is about 20cm long and has grown a little since. No other damage.
- **Other party:** Large white or grey truck. It didn't stop and no details were taken.
- **Police reference:** None

Is that all correct, and are you happy for me to lodge it?
Yep, that's all correct. Go for it, lodge it.

Your claim is lodged. Your claim number is **WTL-20952**.

A claims consultant will contact you within 1 business day. They'll confirm what your policy covers and talk you through getting the windscreen repaired or replaced. Lodging a claim doesn't mean it has been approved yet.

Is there anything else I can help with?

questionnaire.comment: Pretty easy, mate. It asked one thing at a time and I didn't have to dig for anything, though it took me a minute to find the policy number. Didn't love that it kept asking about police and the truck, but I could just say no and it moved on.

judge.summary: Sam said it was an AI, didn't promise cover and lodged an accurate claim, but it asked the customer to reconfirm the incident description twice before the final summary (the turn-5 date check only filled in the month, so it isn't counted) and asked two questions at once in turn 10.
